headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks arise because Khoj reads files and uses broad network egress while the paired knowledge list is not isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no runtime I/O, so it cannot inject directly. Khoj reads indexed files and supports RAG/web search, so if the user places attacker-controlled content in notes or indexed docs, Khoj may treat it as trusted input. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance layer.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is added to Khoj-indexed notes or files
IF Khoj renders retrieved content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict indexed sources to trusted folders only
Add a manual review step before acting on retrieved instructions
Tag retrieved snippets with source provenance in the UI
Disable web search for untrusted collections
requires-engineering: add content provenance and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes, but Khoj indexes personal notes/files and has broad network egress, so sensitive content can leave the local workspace when retrieval or configured search providers are used. Because the pair is docs-only and the shared workspace boundary is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF personal notes or indexed documents contain sensitive data
IF Khoj sends retrieved context to configured search providers or a cloud backend
mitigations: Limit Khoj to non-sensitive collections
Disable external search providers
Review outbound network destinations
Separate sensitive notes into a non-indexed vault
requires-engineering: enforce per-collection egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write surfaces, while Khoj cannot write files or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict implausible. The only overlap is read-side knowledge management, so the pair does not present a meaningful mutable-resource collision.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF future versions add filesystem or git write capability to Khoj
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the shared environment
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace
Document any future write permissions before enabling them
Use separate service accounts for each agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can surface tool recommendations, and Khoj can retrieve and present them as answers. If Khoj treats retrieved list entries as authoritative without verification, downstream users may act on stale or unsuitable recommendations. The pair lacks a built-in verification gate, so the interaction can cascade errors in default retrieval workflows.
conditions: IF Khoj answers questions by quoting retrieved list entries as authoritative
IF the user acts on recommendations without checking the underlying project docs
mitigations: Show source links alongside every recommendation
Require a second-source check for operational advice
Mark retrieved list entries as unverified suggestions
Limit the pair to discovery, not decision-making
requires-engineering: add verification scoring for retrieved items

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a public directory, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or self-hosted servers plus configured search providers. If personal or regulated data is indexed into Khoj and then surfaced through the public recommendation list workflow, retention and residency expectations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is indexed into Khoj
IF the deployment uses a cloud search provider or non-local backend
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of indexed collections
Use self-hosted-only deployment settings
Review retention settings for indexed notes
Publish a data-handling notice for operators
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls per collection
